name: Khalid
story_so_far: After our ship sank in a storm, five of us—Noura, Faisal, Salem, Reem, and I—washed up on this island. We set up Beach Camp by a stream. Initially, Faisal was our provider, but now he, Noura, and I are all sidelined by injuries, leaving only Salem and Reem to hunt and gather. Food is critically scarce. Today, Salem only found one unit of food, and Reem spent the day in the jungle. I have promised Noura I will protect her share of whatever we find, even as my own health declines. My strength is fading rapidly; I am currently at a breaking point due to hunger. The pressure on Salem and Reem is immense, and I fear our survival is hanging by a thread.

Noura.note: I feel a deep responsibility to her, but her extreme weakness and my inability to help her are breaking my heart.

Faisal.note: He was once our backbone, but now that he is injured too, our ability to survive is almost gone.

Salem.note: He is trying, but his small find today only increased my terror about our future.

Reem.note: She is working hard, but I worry if her efforts will be enough to keep us all alive.

plans: I will try to rest and conserve what little energy I have left, hoping Reem returns with something substantial so I can fulfill my promise to Noura.

diary.text: Today was a blur of exhaustion and uncertainty. I tried to take some initiative by looking for food, but the beach yielded nothing once I started searching. It's strange being here with people I don't even know. I hope Faisal, Salem, and Noura are safe in the jungle; it feels dangerous to be alone. I'm hungry, but at least we have a little food left for now.

Today was a bit more productive, but the atmosphere feels heavier. Noura is hurt; her ankle is badly twisted, and seeing her in pain makes me realize how fragile we all are. I managed to find some more food and a piece of wood in the jungle, which feels like a small victory. Faisal also contributed by finding wood for a fire. I'm worried about our food supply, though, as we have to make sure Noura is fed while she can't help.

Today was a bit harder; the jungle didn't yield any food for me, which makes me anxious about our dwindling supplies. I'm glad Faisal and Salem were able to find more wood, though. We are down to only one unit of food left for the group, and with Noura still unable to move, the pressure is mounting. I feel the exhaustion setting in, but I can't let myself slip into despair. We have to keep the fire in mind.

My body aches in ways I didn't expect; this twisted ankle is a heavy burden. I feel so helpless lying here while the others search for food. I gave my last bit of food to Noura because I couldn't bear to see her starve, but now my own stomach is cramping from hunger. I am so tired, and the weakness is starting to set in. I just hope tomorrow brings some good news from the jungle or the reef.

My body feels heavier than it did yesterday, and the pain in my ankle is a constant, throbbing reminder of my helplessness. Salem brought one unit of food this morning, but seeing how empty the reef and the searches were today has left me deeply unsettled. I feel a hollow ache in my stomach that is becoming hard to ignore. I am terrified that if we don't find a steady source of food soon, we won't have the strength to keep the fire going or signal a ship.

Today was devastating. Now Faisal is also down with a twisted ankle, leaving only Salem and Reem to carry the burden of our survival. Noura is so weak she's dizzy, and my own body feels like it's failing me; the hunger is a constant, gnawing predator. I promised Noura I would protect her share, but with so little food, I feel the weight of that promise crushing me. I am terrified that we are running out of time and strength.

My head is spinning, and every breath feels heavy. Today brought even less hope than yesterday; Salem only found one unit of food, and Reem has been gone in the jungle for hours. I am so hungry it feels like a physical ache in my bones, yet I can't think of myself. I keep looking at Noura, seeing her eyes grow hollow, and I feel like a failure for not being able to provide. If nothing changes tomorrow, I don't know if I'll have the strength to even wake up.
